h1: The 4 Best Bissell Cordless Vacuums of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Bissell Cordless Vacuums: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: four Bissell PowerClean cordless vacuums, from the 200W base model to the 280W DualBrush, with runtimes and what separates them.
summary: The Bissell PowerClean FurGuard 280W is the best Bissell cordless vacuum, adding more wattage and a 50 minute runtime to a confirmed cordless body. The DualBrush matches its numbers but does not state cordless. For smaller homes and tighter budgets, the base PowerClean 200W costs the least.
intro: Bissell sells several PowerClean vacuums that look nearly identical on the shelf, and the model names mostly hint at pet features or brush type. The numbers that actually separate them are wattage and runtime. Ignore the badge on the side and read the spec line.

We reviewed four self-standing Bissell cordless models and ranked them on the figures in their listings: motor wattage, runtime, whether the listing confirms cordless operation, and price tier. Where a listing offers no number, we left it blank instead of guessing. The result is a narrow field in which wattage tells most of the story.

products.name: Bissell PowerClean FurGuard 280W Self-Standing Cordless Vacuum
products.verdict: 280W and a 50 minute runtime in a self-standing cordless body.
products.description:
The FurGuard is a self-standing cordless vacuum rated at 280W, with a listed 50 minute runtime. It sits in the $200 to $500 price tier. The pet-oriented name signals a focus on hair, though the listing figures are what we ranked on.

It ranks first because it combines the higher wattage with the longer runtime and an explicit cordless label. Next to the DualBrush, the main difference is certainty: both list 280W and 50 minutes, but only the FurGuard confirms it runs without a cord. Compared with the 200W models, it brings 80W more and 10 extra minutes.

Buy it for a pet household or a larger home where you do not want to stop to recharge. Skip it if you want the lowest price, because this is one of the most expensive of the four.

products.name: Bissell PowerClean DualBrush 280W Self-Standing Vacuum
products.verdict: The same 280W and 50 minutes with a DualBrush design.
products.description:
The DualBrush is a self-standing Bissell rated at 280W with a listed 50 minute runtime, in the $200 to $500 tier. The name points to a two-brush cleaning head.

It ranks second because its numbers are identical to the FurGuard's while the listing does not state cordless operation. That is a real gap when you are buying a stick-style vacuum for the stairs, where a cord is a dealbreaker. The rest of the specs line up, so this is a ranking decided by confirmation, not by raw power.

Buy it if you specifically want the DualBrush design and you have verified the cordless status with the seller. Skip it if a confirmed cordless body matters, since the FurGuard gives you that for the same tier and power.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want the DualBrush model.

products.name: Bissell PowerClean FurFinder 200W Self-Standing Cordless Vacuum
products.verdict: A 200W FurFinder with a 40 minute runtime.
products.description:
The FurFinder is a 200W self-standing cordless vacuum with a listed 40 minute runtime. It falls in the $200 to $500 tier, the same bracket as the 280W models.

It lands third because it gives up 80W and 10 minutes against the leaders without a lower price to compensate. That is the awkward part of this model: the pet-focused name suggests a premium, but the specs say mid-tier. The base PowerClean below it has identical wattage and runtime for less money.

Buy it if you like the pet focus and have a small to medium home where 40 minutes is enough. Skip it if you want the best power per dollar, because the FurGuard offers far more for the same tier and the base PowerClean offers the same for less.
products.skipIf: You want more power for the money.

products.name: Bissell PowerClean 200W Self-Standing Cordless Vacuum
products.verdict: The base 200W PowerClean with 40 minutes of runtime.
products.description:
The base PowerClean is a 200W self-standing cordless vacuum with a listed 40 minute runtime. It carries the lowest price of the four, in the $100 to $200 tier. There is no pet branding on the name.

It ranks last on power, since it shares the lowest wattage with the FurFinder, but it wins the value argument within that pair. The FurFinder matches its runtime and costs more, so unless the pet features speak to you, this is the smarter way to buy the lower-power Bissell.

Buy it for a small home, apartment or quick daily touch-ups where 40 minutes of runtime covers the job. Skip it if you have a lot of carpet or heavy shedding, because 200W is the minimum rating in this group.

whatMatters.detail: Wattage is a rough indicator of motor power, and these models list either 200W or 280W. It matters because a stronger motor generally pulls harder at the floor, but the number alone does not guarantee cleaning performance. Find it in the title or bullets. FurGuard and DualBrush list 280W.

Runtime is how long one charge lasts, from 40 minutes on the FurFinder and base PowerClean to 50 on the FurGuard and DualBrush. A short runtime means stopping mid-clean in a big home. Look for the minutes in the title or bullets, and remember that figures are the seller's.

A self-standing design lets the vacuum stay upright on its own when you pause to move furniture or answer the door. It saves you from laying the machine down or propping it against a wall. All four models here are listed as self-standing. Confirm it in the title.

Cordless operation frees you from outlets and cords, which helps on stairs and in cars, but it needs charging. Confirm that cordless is listed in the description. The FurGuard, FurFinder and base PowerClean say cordless, while the DualBrush listing does not state it.

Pet features such as the FurGuard and FurFinder names suggest hair-handling tools, but names are marketing. What matters is the actual brush design and the figures in the bullets. Check the bullets for brush details and read owner feedback on pet hair if you have shedding animals at home.

faq.a: Three are listed cordless: the FurGuard, FurFinder and base PowerClean. The DualBrush listing does not state it, so confirm with the seller before ordering if you need a cord-free vacuum for stairs.

Buying a FurFinder expecting the strength of a FurGuard. The FurFinder is rated at 200W and 40 minutes, while the FurGuard offers 280W and 50 minutes in the same $200 to $500 tier. Compare the wattage, not the model name.

faq.q: Is the FurGuard worth it over the base model?
faq.a: It adds 80W and 10 minutes of runtime, plus confirmed cordless operation. If your home is larger or you have heavy shedding, that is a meaningful upgrade over the base PowerClean. In a small apartment the base model may be enough.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Charge the battery fully before the first use, then follow the manual for attaching tools and mounting the self-standing body. Check the charging time in the paperwork, as it varies between the PowerClean models.

Empty the dust bin after each session and clean the brush of hair and fibers. On the FurGuard and FurFinder, pet hair wraps quickly, so check the roller often. Rinse washable filters and let them dry fully before refitting.

The base PowerClean 200W is the cheapest, in the $100 to $200 tier, while the other three sit in the $200 to $500 tier. It shares its 40 minute runtime with the FurFinder, so it is the better value of that pair.

finalTake: For most buyers the Bissell PowerClean FurGuard 280W is the cordless pick, with the strongest wattage, the longest runtime and a confirmed cordless body. The DualBrush matches the numbers if you can verify the cord-free claim. Choose the base PowerClean 200W when the budget is tight and your home is small, and skip the FurFinder unless you want its pet focus.
